title: Chris Kelly and Kid Howard
summary: Chris Kelly as a well-liked blues player with a derby; Howard, once a drummer, learned from Chris.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Well, now, can you tell me about Chris Kelly and what he sounded like?

Well, Chris Kelly was a great man. He was great. But I mean, he's not to comparison, you know, with Buddy, you know what I mean? And Chris had lots of jobs around here, because I worked with Chris Van a long time too. And he had plenty of jobs and people liked it, Chris. Chris was a well-liked man. And he did nice around here, he really did nice.
And he was a good blues player.

He was a fine blues player, yes. He's another one, he had that derby, and when he started them blues, you know what I mean? He put that derby on there and make them the wah-wah, and you know, different tones come out of there like that. He was great. Yes.

Yeah. Of course, is that record which you made with Bill Russell there, with Kid Howard, where he plays on more on one of the numbers anyway, the Careless Love, which is supposed to be kind of close to the way Chris played that.

Well, it's a symbol. You see, you take Howard now. Howard is more closer to Chris than anyone of them, you know what I mean? Because him and Chris used to be together all the time. See, Howard was a drummer. See, and then Chris taught him a whole lot, see. And that's where he'd try to pick up Chris Kelly's style, you know. But he did pretty nice. He did pretty nice. He was good. He was a strong man, you know what I mean? Trumpets. He'd go up there and get them higher notes. Howard did. Oh, yeah. He'd get them. He had some of that Armstrong stuff.
Yes, yes. He got some Armstrong stuff. That's what he had. Sure did.
